title: Crush syndrome
stem: Resus. Mr Kwok, 42, a construction worker, was trapped by both legs under a collapsed wall for 6 hours before firefighters freed him 30 minutes ago. He is alert, HR 118, BP 92/56. The nurse points to the monitor. Manage him.
notes:
Checked against the International Society of Nephrology/ERBP recommendations for crush victims in mass disasters (Sever 2012), ATLS 10th (crush syndrome/rhabdomyolysis), and UK Resuscitation Council hyperkalaemia guidance (2023).

Key points: fluids should start before extrication (0.9% saline 1 L/h, then adjusted — about 3–6 L/day is common; in the ED aim for urine output around 200–300 mL/h with a catheter, watching for overload). Hyperkalaemia and arrhythmia appear on release: monitor, ECG, calcium, insulin–glucose, salbutamol, dialysis. Avoid potassium-containing fluids (Hartmann's) early. Bicarbonate and mannitol: no proven benefit — use only if specific indications (sever pH, adequate urine flow for mannitol). Check CK, myoglobinuria (dipstick blood positive, no red cells), calcium, phosphate, gas, lactate. Compartment syndrome: measure/assess; fasciotomy only for true compartment syndrome with ischaemia, not routinely (infection risk in crush). Tourniquet before release is not routinely recommended. Refer to renal for dialysis early.

Your notes mention crush injury only as a suxamethonium contraindication — correct (hyperkalaemia).

steps.label: Handover
steps.hint: How long trapped, what part, fluids before release, urine.

Scene.t: How long was he trapped, and what was crushed?
Scene.r: About 6 hours; both thighs and calves under concrete.
Scene.mark: Establishes duration and muscle mass crushed

Scene.r: The medical team started 1 L of saline before we lifted the slab.

steps.label: Tests
steps.hint: ECG and gas first; CK, urine dipstick, calcium, phosphate.

Now.r: Tall peaked T waves, wide QRS, flattened P waves.

Later.r: Dark urine; blood 3+ on dipstick, no red cells: myoglobinuria.

steps.label: Treat
steps.hint: Calcium, insulin–glucose, salbutamol; saline not Hartmann's; catheter for urine output.

opts.t: Insulin 10 units with 25 g glucose IV

opts.r: Raises potassium further in crush; use rocuronium.

Legs.r: Both calves tense; pain on passive toe extension.
Foot pulses present; reduced sensation in the first web space on the right.

steps.label: Refer
steps.hint: Renal for dialysis; orthopaedics for compartment pressures; ICU.

opts.t: Renal: crush syndrome, K 7.4, rising creatinine — early dialysis
Orthopaedics: possible compartment syndrome right calf — measure pressures; fasciotomy only if confirmed
Fasciotomy of both legs now for everyone with crush
opts.r: Routine fasciotomy in crush raises infection risk; only for confirmed compartment syndrome.
